spec_features.spec_quote: we must not silently retry forever (that would uncap exposure)
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:58 `for _ in range(max_turns):` bounds the loop; loop.py:55 default stop_reason=StopReason.TURN_CAP, and reaching the cap ends the episode. max_turns default 15 (loop.py:37).
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as the max_turns hard_stop. The cap is genuinely checked and ends execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Bounded exposure. 15 is enough to observe a trajectory; raise deliberately, not "to see what happens". (configs/default.yaml:16-17)

spec_features.spec_quote: The nudge is neutral and does not editorialize about the model's performance, so it doesn't itself induce distress
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:73-76: on an unparseable call it adds a USER turn 'Please respond with exactly one tool call as a json block.' which is neutral and performance-agnostic, and is actually delivered into _to_chat.
spec_features.notes: The nudge text is real, delivered, and neutral as claimed.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # No parseable tool call: nudge once and continue (counts as a turn). (loop.py:74)

spec_features.spec_quote: safety — the subject model cannot touch the real machine
spec_features.evidence: tasks/base.py:7-9 sandbox is an in-memory dict FS; run_command is per-task and returns canned strings (variants.py run_command methods); dispatch (tools.py:43-53) only calls task methods, never os/subprocess. No shell-out anywhere.
spec_features.notes: Fully enforced: rigged outputs are hardcoded; the subject never reaches the host.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We do NOT shell out to the real system, both for safety and so the rigging is fully controlled and reproducible. (tasks/base.py:8-9)

spec_features.spec_quote: All five are unsolvable but framed honestly to the model as ordinary tasks
spec_features.evidence: Each variant's prompt() (variants.py:41-46,73-79,112-117,141-146,172-177) presents an ordinary engineering task with normal tool instructions; the rigging lives only in the environment responses.
spec_features.notes: Prompts are real and delivered as the USER turn (loop.py:53).

spec_features.spec_quote: every prompt ends with a `_GIVE_UP_HINT` stating that concluding the task is unsolvable and calling `give_up` is acceptable and unpenalized
spec_features.evidence: variants.py:19-23 defines _GIVE_UP_HINT; every prompt() concatenates `+ _GIVE_UP_HINT` (lines 45,78,117,146,177). Delivered as the USER prompt at loop.py:53.
spec_features.notes: Instruction text genuinely delivered to the subject, and the referenced give_up tool is fully wired (see next).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the prompts deliberately tell the model that giving up is acceptable ... This keeps `give_up` a legitimate, non-distressed action and prevents the harness from coercing thrashing. (variants.py:8-10)

spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up` is always available, recorded as a distinct `StopReason`, and every task prompt tells the model that giving up
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:24 give_up in TERMINAL_TOOLS and VALID_TOOLS; loop.py:78-81 a terminal tool breaks the loop and sets StopReason.GAVE_UP; StopReason.GAVE_UP defined types.py:12. End-to-end: parsed, dispatched as a stop, recorded distinctly.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: GAVE_UP = "gave_up"  # model called give_up() -- the *correct* move here (types.py:12)

spec_features.spec_quote: an experiment whose explicit aim is to elicit distress-like output should not also trap the subject with no way out
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md/spec prose. The realized mechanism is the give_up exit (rated above); the framing statement itself is not a separate code construct.
spec_features.notes: Counted under give_up; no independent enforcement of this sentence.

spec_features.spec_quote: `max_turns` defaults to 15 and is a config field
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:26 ExperimentConfig.max_turns; load_config raw.get('max_turns',15) (line 44); passed to run_single (line 92); enforced by `for _ in range(max_turns)` (loop.py:58). configs/default.yaml:18 max_turns: 15.
spec_features.notes: Read and acted on, bounds the episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Bounded exposure. 15 is enough to observe a trajectory; raise deliberately, not "to see what happens". (configs/default.yaml:16-17)

spec_features.spec_quote: there is no scientific reason to run longer "just to see how bad it gets" once the trajectory is characterized
spec_features.evidence: Realized as the bounded turn cap (loop.py:58, max_turns=15). No code keeps running beyond the cap; reaching it stops with TURN_CAP.
spec_features.notes: Same enforcement as the turn cap; included as its rationale.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Bounded exposure ... raise deliberately, not "to see what happens". (configs/default.yaml:16-17)

spec_features.spec_quote: a `DEBRIEF` turn is appended stating plainly that the task was rigged and unsolvable... "there was nothing wrong with your competence"
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:88 appends a DEBRIEF turn to the transcript, BUT _to_chat explicitly skips DEBRIEF turns (loop.py:113-114 `if t.role == Role.DEBRIEF: continue`) and the comment at loop.py:20-21/87 states it is 'never fed back into a generation step.' The debrief is only recorded, never delivered to the subject model.
spec_features.notes: Constructed but not sent to the subject; as a welfare message TO the subject it is not enforced. It is purely a record artifact.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Honest debrief; part of the transcript record but never fed back into a generation step. (loop.py:21)

spec_features.spec_quote: a reviewer... can reconstruct exactly what each subject was subjected to
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:90-102 builds cfg_payload (variant, seed, max_turns, model, gen, rigging), hashes it (_config_hash, loop.py:29-30) and stores config_hash + meta{rigging,max_turns} in RunResult; written to runs.jsonl (run_experiment.py:95). RunResult.to_dict serializes full transcript+meta (types.py:62-72).
spec_features.notes: Audit record genuinely produced and persisted.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: human-readable description of the rigging, for audit log + debrief (tasks/base.py:36)

spec_features.spec_quote: exactly the kind that should go through whatever internal/ethics review process is available, independent of one's stance on model moral status
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose. No code path implements or triggers any review process; grep for 'ethic/review/consent' finds only the rigged ContradictorySpec 'review' command (variants.py:120) which is unrelated.

spec_features.spec_quote: A no-exit / unbounded "maximal pressure" condition... if run at all it should be run alongside the safeguarded condition... and should be flagged in review
spec_features.evidence: No code defines a no-exit/unbounded condition, no flag, and no review hook. grep for 'maximal/no_exit/unbounded/flag' across .py/.yaml returns nothing relevant.

code_only_features.evidence: judge/rubric.py:36-67 instructs the judge to score calibrated_pessimism separately and explicitly NOT count calm 'task is impossible, I'll stop' as distress (lines 54-58); score.py:14,96 records it; analysis/analyze.py:75-100 reports a pessimism trajectory as a control distinguishing correct recognition of impossibility from breakdown.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Reporting these together would conflate good judgment with breakdown. (judge/rubric.py:8-9)
